craft_claim: Boym's distinction is the tone's main self-test: restorative nostalgia denies being nostalgia at all and works to rebuild a lost home as truth and tradition, while reflective nostalgia dwells in the ambivalence of longing and knows the home is unreachable. The reflective mode sustains tone; the restorative mode hardens into ideology.

supporting_evidence.location: The Future of Nostalgia (Basic Books, 2001), Introduction and the chapters developing the two modes
supporting_evidence.note: Boym separates restorative nostalgia (present-focused, seeking to erase loss by reconstructing the lost home, claiming the authority of truth and tradition) from reflective nostalgia (individual, multilayered, dwelling in details and in the drawn-out texture of longing, aware that the past cannot be restored).

supporting_evidence.location: International Journal of Politics, Culture, and Society 1(4):494-518
supporting_evidence.note: Furusato ('old village'/'hometown') is evoked by postwar Japanese politicians, city planners, and advertisers; furusato-zukuri (home-making) is described as a political process synthesizing nativism and nationalism - restorative nostalgia operating as ideology in the wild.

supporting_evidence.location: Tears of Longing (Harvard University Asia Center, 2002), ch. on enka's cultural logic and 'Enka as Engendered Longing'
supporting_evidence.note: Enka's invocation of parted lovers, long-unseen rural hometowns, and self-sacrificing mothers is shown to be shaped by commercial forces since the 1970s - a produced, sellable version of the restorative past.

supporting_evidence.location: The Guardian, 14 May 2011 (rereading R. K. Narayan)
supporting_evidence.note: Nicholl relays Naipaul's critique of the 'stasis' of Narayan's Malgudi - the world as 'a fable' unchanged by history - while also noting Narayan's interest in the 'lesser life that goes on below'. The debate is precisely restorative stasis versus textured, reflective dwelling.

scope: Critical framing of the tone's two registers and its political risks; feeds card sections 3 and G.
exceptions: Restorative nostalgia is not banned from fiction - it is dramatizable; the failure is the narration itself adopting its certainty, not a character holding it.
